summary: The transport layer provides process-to-process delivery using port numbers. It covers two main protocols: TCP and UDP. TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, delivers data in order, and includes flow control, congestion control, and a header size of 20 to 60 bytes, making it suitable for HTTP/HTTPS, email, and file transfer. UDP is connectionless, unreliable, faster, has a low fixed header size of 8 bytes, and is used for DNS queries, gaming, live video, and VoIP. The rule of thumb is to choose TCP when every byte must arrive correctly and in order, and UDP when low delay matters more than losing a few packets.

key_terms.definition: The transport layer provides process-to-process delivery using port numbers.
Port numbers are used by the transport layer to provide process-to-process delivery.
TCP is a connection-oriented, reliable protocol that delivers data in order, uses flow and congestion control, and has a header size of 20 to 60 bytes.
A three-way handshake using SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK sets up a connection before TCP data is sent.
Flow control uses a sliding window so that a fast sender does not overwhelm a slow receiver.
Congestion control makes the sender slow down when the network is congested.
UDP is a connectionless, unreliable protocol with a fixed 8-byte header that is faster and has lower delay than TCP.
Choose TCP when every byte must arrive correctly and in order, and choose UDP when low delay matters more than losing a few packets.
